resources.string: What is sent: To check, Robot asks GitHub (api.github.com) for the repository\'s newest releases, and it downloads an update from GitHub\'s servers. GitHub sees your IP address and Robot\'s version in the request; nothing else is sent. An access token, if you add one, goes to api.github.com only.\n\nWhat is checked: Before installing, Robot checks the file\'s SHA-256 against the release\'s SHA256SUMS, then that it is Robot, the release\'s version, newer than this one, and signed with Robot\'s key. Android\'s own window then asks you to confirm.

Only for a private repository: a fine-grained token that can read its contents, or a classic one with the repo scope. Robot encrypts it on this phone and sends it to api.github.com only.

Tell the developer about a bug or an idea. Robot puts your words and what you tick into one plain-text message, and you send it with the app you choose: your SMS or messaging app, for example. Robot sends nothing itself.

What goes is exactly what Preview shows: your words, Robot\'s version, this phone and its Android build, the model and the look, and only what you tick. What Robot adds is codes, numbers and switches: never your conversations or History, transcripts, messages, memory, People or contacts, notes, calendar, a wake phrase\'s words (a phrase is its number), a helper\'s name, address or key, the updater\'s repository or token, a Wi-Fi or Bluetooth name, or where you are.\n\nShare opens Android\'s share sheet: pick the app and the developer. Long messages may arrive as several texts. Copy marks the message as sensitive and clears it from the clipboard after a minute if nothing else replaced it. Your draft stays until you tap Done.

Share opens Android\'s share sheet: pick your SMS or messaging app, and the developer. Text it opens your SMS app with %1$s filled in; you press Send there.

Opens a new issue in your browser with the message filled in, cut to about 7,000 characters if it is longer. GitHub receives the message when the page opens, whether or not you submit the issue. A private repository needs you signed in to GitHub there.
